quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: You are driving on a two-lane road with no bike lanes and see a cyclist ahead going the same direction. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic. Then pass the cyclist with plenty of space.
Keep driving straight. The cyclist must get out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic light or stop sign.
Honk to warn the cyclist that you are about to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic. Then pass the cyclist with plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Pass a cyclist like you would pass any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space between your mirror and the cyclist, or 5 feet on faster roads or with multiple cyclists. Do not honk suddenly—it may startle them and cause a crash.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and cyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before turning across tracks. Obey all signs and traffic signals. Light rail trains share the road with cars and cyclists.

questions.question: A cyclist who breaks traffic laws:

options.text: Is allowed to break the law because cyclists do not have to follow traffic laws.
Can be ticketed.
Will always get just a warning from police.
Will have their bike taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Cyclists have the same rights, duties, and responsibilities as car drivers. Both car drivers and cyclists who break traffic laws can be ticketed.

questions.question: If your wheels drop onto the road shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, reduce your speed without hard braking. Then carefully turn back onto the road. Watch for other traffic when you re-enter.

questions.question: A space cushion around your car should be kept:

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive close to vehicles on your left and right.

questions.question: From top to bottom, the correct order for a traffic light is:

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.
Green, yellow, red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: Red is always on top and green on the bottom for a vertical signal. For a horizontal signal, red is always on the left and green on the right.

questions.question: Before making a right turn, your car should be:

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you begin turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Move as far to the right as possible before turning right. Do not cross other lanes of traffic to make any turn.

questions.question: When driving in an area where children are playing, expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing.
Run out in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful near children. They may not understand danger and could run into traffic without looking first.

questions.question: When passing on a highway with multiple lanes:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Only pass on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear. Use the proper turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: Drivers cannot pass from either side of a ____ center line.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line in the center of a two-way road means no traffic from either direction can cross it to pass.

questions.question: What do pennant-shaped signs mean?

options.text: School zones.
No passing zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zones.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones. The sign will have text that says no passing.

questions.question: How much space you need to cross traffic depends on what?

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
A stop sign.
Using your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator gets stuck while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral and press the brake pedal with steady pressure. When it is safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered crossing gates.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices tell you to. Not all crossings have gates or flashing lights. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: You are in an accident and someone is injured. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless you have to. Moving them without training can make injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If they are bleeding badly, use direct pressure to stop the bleeding.

questions.question: Which is NOT a factor in how far it takes to stop your vehicle?

options.text: Steering ability
Braking distance
Reaction distance
Perception time

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change with speed and road conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means no U-turns. Do not make a U-turn where this sign is posted.

questions.question: When passing a car on a two-lane road with traffic going both ways, what should you do?

options.text: Return to your lane when you have enough space between you and the car you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road right away.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to your lane when you have enough space between you and the car you passed.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, return to the right side when there is enough space between you and the car you passed.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on the freeway shoulder?

options.text: As long as you turn on your emergency flashers.
If your vehicle is not on the road.
If you need to look at a map.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency.

questions.question: What should you do when a car is coming at you with bright headlights?

options.text: Use your bright lights until they dim theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a car is coming at you with high beams on, look away from the lights and toward the right side of the road until it passes. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic going both ways, you must:

options.text: Not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane road, you must use the oncoming traffic lane to complete your pass. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads, who must yield?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This applies to both controlled and uncontrolled intersections.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you must:

options.text: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and other traffic.
Slow down without stopping completely.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and other traffic.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic. Wait until the intersection is clear before moving forward.

questions.question: Unless posted otherwise, the speed limit in school zones is:

options.text: 10 mph.
20 mph.
30 mph.
50 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 20 mph.
questions.explanation: Unless posted otherwise, you must not drive faster than 20 mph in a school zone. Drive carefully in areas where children and pedestrians may enter the road.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed with care through the intersection.
